100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On October 8, 1926, the United States experienced a significant political shift as President Calvin Coolidge announced he would not seek re-election, fueling speculation about the 1928 presidential race. In Europe, tensions rose as the League of Nations faced criticism over its handling of disputes, particularly regarding the ongoing conflicts in the Balkans. Meanwhile, in the world of entertainment, Chicago's own Al Jolson made headlines with his groundbreaking performance in "The Jazz Singer," heralding a new era in film.
